description:
FILED s506f (Opus, 2026-10-04) per the s506f brief (D4: PERL5OPT is NOT in that batch).

perl reads PERL5OPT and applies its switches as if they preceded the command line (perlrun):
"Command-line options (switches). Switches in this variable are treated as if they were on every Perl
command line. Only the -[CDIMTUWdmtw] switches are allowed."  Anything else dies:
  PERL5OPT=-n perl -e 1   ->  Illegal switch in PERL5OPT: -n
(re-probe the exact text and status before mirroring; also -T in PERL5OPT enables taint and stops
further PERL5OPT processing).

`pcl` ignores PERL5OPT today.  tools/pclperl-for-tests (the harness "perl") DOES prepend it, through
PCLSwitches::parse_argv, without the allowed-subset check.

FIX SHAPE: one function in tools/lib/PCLSwitches.pm (perl5opt_events) parsing $ENV{PERL5OPT} with the
same cluster grammar, refusing a letter outside the subset with perl's message; `pcl` and the wrapper
both prepend its events (one implementation).

THE BREAKING CASE TO PROBE FIRST: an environment that carries `PERL5OPT=-MDevel::Cover` (coverage runs,
CI images) -- every `pcl` run would then `use Devel::Cover`, an XS module PCL cannot load.  Decide (and
write down) whether pcl honours that too (perl's semantics) or announces and skips a -M it cannot load.
Also `PERL5OPT=-w` is common in some CI setups (with -w now = $^W, harmless).
subject: `pcl` does not honour PERL5OPT (perl prepends its switches, a restricted subset -[CDIMTUWdmtw])
